title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is legislation designed to curb the ecological footprint of AI systems, requiring developers to assess and reduce energy consumption, waste, and resource use. It sets standards and reporting obligations so that AI technologies operate sustainably while protecting environmental resources.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that bans artificial intelligence from diagnosing, treating, or otherwise providing medical care, requiring that all such services be performed by licensed human doctors. It sets out legal and regulatory measures to enforce this restriction and safeguard patients from unverified AI medical interventions.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to encourage the export of AI technologies by creating incentives for businesses to sell AI software, hardware, and services overseas. The bill also outlines measures to support domestic AI companies in expanding their global presence and to ensure compliance with U.S. export control regulations.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law that would require AI developers to release key models and algorithms as open source, enabling public auditing and collaborative improvement. It aims to foster trust, encourage collaboration among researchers, and reduce the risk of unfair or unsafe AI systems.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 sets out clear rules to govern how AI technologies are developed, tested, and deployed for veterans, ensuring that these tools are transparent, fair, and respectful of privacy. It establishes oversight mechanisms, impact‑assessment requirements, and ethical standards so that AI systems serving veterans are safe, accountable, and aligned with the unique needs of the veteran community.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act establishes guidelines and standards for securing advanced artificial‑intelligence systems, urging developers to embed robust safety and security measures from the earliest stages of design. It promotes collaboration among industry, academia, and government to assess risks, conduct audits, and share best practices, thereby protecting critical infrastructure and sensitive data from AI‑related threats.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 seeks to reduce bias in AI decision‑making by requiring developers to assess, mitigate, and document discriminatory impacts in their algorithms. It establishes guidelines and reporting obligations to promote fairness and accountability in algorithmic systems.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a federal law designed to curb the unauthorized copying and distribution of AI models developed in the United States. It imposes strict penalties, requires robust security measures, and establishes regulatory oversight to protect the intellectual property rights of AI developers.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 proposes that companies must evaluate and disclose how their algorithms affect people, especially in areas like hiring, lending, and policing. It aims to make algorithmic decision‑making more transparent, fair, and safe by requiring impact assessments, testing, and oversight.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This act requires the Department of Defense to rigorously test and validate AI systems before they are used in military operations. It also mandates regular reporting on the performance, safety incidents, and potential risks of these AI systems to ensure accountability and transparency.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law designed to establish a framework that ensures artificial intelligence systems are developed, deployed, and overseen in a transparent, fair, and safe manner. It calls for regular impact assessments, accountability requirements, and enforcement mechanisms to mitigate risks such as bias, discrimination, and privacy violations.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act mandates AI developers and operators to regularly publish detailed reports on the power consumption, energy efficiency, and performance metrics of their AI systems. This transparency framework is designed to help regulators assess environmental impact, promote responsible AI development, and compare technologies across the industry.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law designed to stop AI from misleading voters by making it mandatory that any political content created with artificial intelligence clearly states that it is AI-generated. It also sets penalties for using AI to produce deceptive political messages that could influence election outcomes.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a proposed law that seeks to regulate autonomous AI systems capable of self‑enhancement. It requires continuous monitoring, safety checks, and accountability measures so that such systems operate transparently and do not pose risks to society.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on the construction and operation of new AI data centers. The goal is to allow policymakers to assess and address environmental, energy, and societal impacts before allowing such facilities to resume development.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is designed to shield households from the rising utility bills generated by the growing energy demands of AI data centers. It proposes stricter energy‑efficiency standards and potential subsidies to keep these costs from disproportionately impacting families.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act imposes a temporary halt on the approval, construction, and expansion of new AI data centers. This pause is meant to give lawmakers time to assess the environmental, economic, and security impacts of large-scale AI infrastructure before moving forward.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law that seeks to bring clearer rules around the development and use of artificial intelligence. It aims to lift uncertainty by setting out requirements for transparency, safety, and accountability so that AI systems can be used responsibly and in the public interest.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 is designed to protect kids from risks associated with AI‑powered toys, setting clear safety and data‑privacy standards that all such products must meet. It requires manufacturers to comply with rigorous testing and oversight, ensuring toys are safe to use, free from harmful content, and respect children’s personal information.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a proposed law designed to protect the personal data of minors when they interact with AI technologies. It likely sets rules and limits on how AI systems can collect, use, or share information about young users.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act likely mandates the collection and reporting of data on AI development and deployment across the country, aiming to provide a comprehensive overview of the nation's AI capabilities. It probably establishes guidelines for transparency, accountability, and regulatory oversight to ensure responsible use of AI technologies.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a proposed law that sets rules for how AI models should be created, tested, and used so that they are safe and fair. It requires companies to explain how their AI works, keep data secure, and be accountable if the AI causes problems.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires AI developers to produce and deliver a detailed “bill of materials” that lists all components, data sources, and training processes used in their AI systems, aiming to improve transparency and accountability. It also includes additional provisions—such as safety standards, compliance measures, and regulatory oversight—to ensure responsible AI deployment.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act is designed to build a skilled workforce that supports the development and deployment of trustworthy AI systems. It focuses on training, hiring, and education initiatives that equip workers with the knowledge and skills needed to responsibly create and manage AI technologies.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act aims to curb the rising costs of AI services and protect workers from wage manipulation by establishing regulations against price gouging and wage fixing in the AI industry. It would require companies to maintain fair pricing and transparent labor practices, with penalties for violations.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 sets new rules for using artificial intelligence in agriculture. It aims to protect farmers’ data, promote responsible AI use, and ensure that AI tools in farming are safe and transparent.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act aims to encourage the use of AI technologies within the banking and investment sectors by creating a supportive regulatory framework. It focuses on fostering innovation while ensuring consumer protection, data privacy, and financial stability through clear guidelines and oversight.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is designed to encourage the use of artificial intelligence in banking, insurance, and other financial industries. It proposes guidelines and incentives for firms to responsibly adopt AI technologies while protecting consumers and maintaining market stability.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act is a legislative proposal aimed at fostering the development and retention of skilled professionals in artificial intelligence and related fields. It proposes measures such as increased funding for research and education, incentives for companies to hire AI talent, and initiatives to promote diversity and inclusion within the industry.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The “No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act” would prohibit the construction of AI data centers on any federal property. The law aims to protect national lands from the environmental and security impacts associated with large-scale AI computing infrastructure.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 requires schools to teach students how AI works and how to use it safely, so they can understand and participate in a technology‑driven world. The law also mandates that teachers receive training, schools get the necessary resources, and all students have equal access to AI tools so every child is prepared for future jobs and society.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to give students from kindergarten through 12th grade a solid foundation in artificial intelligence, covering how it works, how it’s used, and the ethical questions it raises. It sets out guidelines for schools to build AI-focused lessons, train teachers, and provide resources so that students can safely and effectively navigate an increasingly AI‑driven world.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 proposes a comprehensive legal framework for artificial intelligence that emphasizes safety, transparency, accountability, and ethical use. It aims to balance innovation with societal protection by establishing regulatory bodies and guidelines for the responsible development and deployment of AI technologies.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act seeks to provide clear guidance to teachers, students, and administrators on the responsible use of AI technologies in educational settings. It establishes standards and best practices for integrating AI tools while protecting student privacy and promoting equitable learning outcomes.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: Every American and community affected by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should be entitled to transparency and local autonomy. The House of Representatives urges that such communities have the right to be informed and involved in decisions regarding AI data center development.
